summary.headline: CMS Info Systems Q1 FY27 services revenue hit a record INR625 crores (+9.3% YoY) despite a INR25 crore currency-supply hit; FY27 EBITDA margin guide raised to about 27%.
summary.overview: Services revenue reached an all-time high of INR625 crores, up 9.3% YoY and 2.6% QoQ, but was INR25 crores below the company's internal run-rate target of INR650 crores because banks supplied only about 70% of indented currency. EBITDA rose 8.9% YoY to INR173 crores with margin up 170 bps QoQ to 27.2%, while EBIT fell to INR32 crores (10.3% margin) on higher depreciation from HAWKAI/ALGO capex and the FSS acquisition. Management trimmed FY27 services revenue guidance to INR2,650-2,750 crores (from INR2,700-2,800 crores) and raised the EBITDA margin guide to about 27% (from 25-26%). Currency fulfilment has since recovered to roughly 80-85% of indents, and management expects normalisation by end-Q2.

financial_highlights.change: vs 14.1% margin a year ago; would be ~15% excluding INR18 crore BLA revenue impact
-10.6% YoY, +5.8% QoQ; PAT margin -170 bps YoY, +70 bps QoQ
lower due to deferred tax gain from Securens turnaround

financial_highlights.value: 49.39 lakh shares at INR340, INR168 crores total

segments.name: ATM / BLA (brown label, transaction-linked)
segments.commentary: Revenue impact of about INR18 crores from currency shortage; ATMs at about 70% supply saw transactions fall 27% YoY while well-supplied ATMs were flat. This segment is about 12% of revenue and management will not invest incremental capital in it.

segments.name: Cash Logistics (work for other MSPs)
segments.commentary: Revenue impact of about INR7 crores from the currency shortage.

segments.name: Technology and Payments (HAWKAI, ALGO MVS)
segments.commentary: Now 18% of services revenue in Q1 (7% in FY22, 16% in FY26), with a target of above 20% by end-Q4 FY27. Guided to grow 35-40% in FY27; ALGO MVS deployed at SBI and due to go live at ICICI in Q3.

segments.name: FSS acquisition
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR20 crores of accrual in Q1 with contracts still being novated; synergies expected from H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 services revenue raised? No: trimmed to INR2,650-2,750 crores from INR2,700-2,800 crores; total revenue INR2,750-2,850 crores.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided to about 27%, up from 25-26% guided in May.

Platform growth FY27: ATM Management and Retail & Currency Logistics 11-14%; Technology and Payments 35-40%; combined services revenue growth 15-19%. Another remark cited 10-13% for ATM and retail platforms.
FY27 capex INR100-125 crores (vs peak INR350 crores in FY26 and ~INR200 crores average); could rise but should not exceed INR200 crores if tech opportunities materialise.
Depreciation ratio expected to improve in H2 FY27 and be better in FY28.
Currency fulfilment expected to normalise by end-Q2; IBA committee update on PSU repricing expected by end-Q2; private sector repricing targeted to close by Q2.
Cash conversion of 65-70% of EBITDA maintained; about INR400 crores cash on books, with surplus to be returned via dividend or buyback at year-end review.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was INR350 crores, mainly for order execution and HAWKAI/ALGO product development; FY27 guided to INR100-125 crores, mainly tech.
Tech spend held at 1.5% of revenue.
Around 70,000 ATMs and 65,000 retail touchpoints; more than 50% of ATM touchpoints now under end-to-end integrated contracts.
Won INR500 crores of orders in Q1, including HDFC Bank (6,000 ATMs over 5 years, TCV INR400 crores); 2 ATM recycler RFPs (about 1,000 recyclers) to be executed by year-end.
demand_pricing: Currency supply to banks fell to about 70% of indents in April-May; recovered to about 80-85% now. Currency in circulation up 12% YoY, which management reads as a supply rather than demand problem.

Steep state minimum wage increases (6% to 60% in certain large states) and fuel costs up 8%; management expects larger-than-average price increases, with private banks and retail customers in progress.
Market share: 60% in ATM cash management and 38% in retail solutions, retained from last year.
Outsourced ATM market share rising to about 60-65% (from about 50% 10 years ago); PSU in-house ATMs about 70,000-75,000 of the roughly 100,000 bank ATMs.
Competition broadening in AI and payments as new entrants arrive; management argues full-stack hardware and software ownership is a moat.
Management stated it will not enter merchant acquiring; it has no plans for a payment aggregator licence.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cash crunch transient or structural, and could banks have deliberately under-supplied low-potential ATMs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the worst is past (supply went from about 70% to 80-85%) and rejected the idea that banks chose which ATMs to starve, describing geographic imbalances instead. Demand is not the problem; the end-Q2 result will show it.

qa_highlights.question: What changes are being made to forecasting after repeated shocks?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajiv Kaul said FY22-24 met or exceeded forecasts while FY25-26 fell short, and the team will keep setting realistic stretch targets. He called the criticism fair and said Q1 shortfall was flagged early.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue came from FSS in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly INR20 crores of accrual, with contracts still being novated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of possible UPI MDR and polymer notes?
qa_highlights.answer: MDR of 30-50 bps is being discussed; cash costs merchants about 10-20 bps. Polymer notes are planned for lower denominations, with limited direct impact as ATMs are not configured for them; possible CIT and processing upside.

qa_highlights.question: How was the INR4,00 crore TAM for HAWKAI derived?
qa_highlights.answer: BFSI: about 400,000 ATMs and branches, with 100,000-120,000 outsourced today, over 5-7 years. Non-BFSI is based on use cases and pilots (gold loan branches, dark stores, warehouses), with a healthy BFSI RFP pipeline over the next 18-24 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBIT margin recovery path and capital allocation view?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation ratio to improve in H2 FY27, with FSS synergies and HAWKAI/ALGO revenue returns expected; full normalisation in FY28. Buyback not revisited until year-end; surplus cash (about INR400 crores) to be returned via dividend or buyback.

risks_watch: Currency fulfilment: banks supplied about 70% of indents in April-May and about 80-85% now; management expects normalisation by end-Q2 and has not put a firm date on it. Track the end-Q2 update and public currency-in-circulation data.

BLA estate exposure: about 12% of revenue is transaction-linked; ATMs at about 70% supply saw transactions fall 27% YoY. Management said it will prune persistently underperforming ATMs if supply and transactions do not improve.

Pricing recovery: state minimum wage hikes (6% to 60% in some large states) and fuel up 8%. Private bank and retail repricing is in progress; PSU repricing depends on the IBA committee, with an update promised by end-Q2.

EBIT and depreciation: EBIT margin fell to 10.3% from 14.1% a year ago on HAWKAI/ALGO and FSS depreciation. Management guided the depreciation ratio to improve in H2 FY27 and be better in FY28; FSS synergies are expected from H2.
Tech and Payments ramp: the segment is guided to grow 35-40% in FY27 and cross 20% of services revenue by end-Q4. Watch ALGO MVS go-live at ICICI in Q3 and the HAWKAI bid pipeline.

Forecasting credibility: management admitted FY25-26 fell short of forecasts after FY22-24 met or exceeded them, and cut FY27 services revenue guidance. Also watch the capital allocation stance, with the buyback not revisited until year-end and about INR400 crores of cash on books.
key_quotes: And the shortfall is entirely down to the worst cash supply squeeze this industry has seen in the last decade.
Now this is not a demand problem. Currency in circulation is up 12% year-on-year.
It's a fair criticism. And if -- as I reflect, and we do reflect on this, just to put context, I think FY22, '23, '24 were 3 years where we met or exceeded all forecast and high growth.
I think we'll look at it only towards the end of the year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, cash and the Tech and Payments growth story, but cautious on currency supply and PSU repricing, where answers stayed open-ended with timing tied to end-Q2. Management was candid about the forecasting misses and the depreciation drag, and evasive on the buyback and on specific PSU renewal timing.
